name: Dementia
remarks: right now this is just Alzheimer's but there are other dementias that could be adapted into this model
Alzheimer's has been shown to be significantly based on genetics, and there are specific genes to point to for early-onset:
https://www.nia.nih.gov/alzheimers/publication/alzheimers-disease-genetics-fact-sheet
Since Synthea does not currently model at the level of individual genes
we'll use a simple probability to differentiate the population into who will and won't get alzheimers.
The 40% chance does seem high, but the key factor here is the delay in when it appears.
38% of people over age 85 have alzheimer's. ( http://www.alzheimers.net/resources/alzheimers-statistics/ )
Early onset Alzheimers affects roughly 5% of people with Alzheimer's. http://www.mayoclinic.org/diseases-conditions/alzheimers-disease/in-depth/alzheimers/art-20048356
There is evidence that higher education leads to a delay in the onset of alzheimers.

Task 5.2: routed via Custom_AD_Dx_Guard instead of straight to DiagnosisEncounter.
CROSS-MODULE GATE (audit Class 7, task 5.2 group 2) -- stock dementia <->
ModSynthea's alzheimers.json. Both modules diagnose SNOMED 26929004 with
no coordination; this module additionally diagnoses 230265002 from the
same encounter. Rule: FIRST-TO-DIAGNOSE WINS. If alzheimers.json has
already diagnosed, this module stands down (Terminal) instead of running a
second, parallel AD course on the same patient.
The test is the ATTRIBUTE `alzheimers_disease`, not Active Condition
26929004, and that is load-bearing. `alzheimers_disease` is assigned by
alzheimers.json's MildDementia ConditionOnset and is written by nothing
else in the tree (verified by grep: the only other hits are alz.org URLs
in this file's own remarks). The code cannot be used at the twin
Custom_AD_Dx_Recheck below, because by the time that state runs THIS
module has just recorded 26929004 itself -- the code test would be true
for every patient. One signal is used at both gates so the two cannot
disagree.
What this closes, in order of importance:
1. EndFirstPrescription. HealthRecord.medicationStart is idempotent per
RxCUI, so this module's FirstPrescription2 (donepezil 997223) and
FirstPrescription1 (galantamine 310436) bind 'Alzheimer's Medication'
to alzheimers.json's ALREADY-OPEN chronic order for the same drug;
EndFirstPrescription then reaches HealthRecord.medicationEnd ->
chronicMedicationEnd and deletes that patient's lifelong ChEI refill
stream (~80% of alzheimers.json's patients are on one of those two
drugs). Blocking DiagnosisEncounter closes this completely:
ModerateDecline only reaches ModeratelySevere_Encounter -- the sole
route to EndFirstPrescription -- on its PriorState DiagnosisEncounter
branch, and Dementia_CarePlan/FirstPrescription* are reachable only
downstream of DiagnosisEncounter.
2. Two parallel dementia care pathways (careplan, MMSE series, ChEI and
memantine arms, staging encounters) billed for one disease.
3. Entry.name corruption on the shared 26929004 condition -- see
Custom_AD_Dx_Recheck.
Not a duplicate condition ROW: HealthRecord.conditionStart is idempotent
per code, so co-diagnosis never produced two 26929004 rows. The audit's
'double diagnosis' framing overstates that part; the damage was the
duplicated pathway and the medication strip.
Timing: DiagnosisEncounter is `wellness: true`, so State.Encounter.process
blocks until the encounter module's next wellness visit -- this guard's
verdict can be up to about a year stale by the time the encounter opens.
Custom_AD_Dx_Recheck re-tests once it has.
This is the enounter where alzheimer's is diagnosed.
Typical life expectancy after an Alzheimer’s diagnosis is 4-to-8 years. (Alzheimer’s Association)
CROSS-MODULE GATE, second half (task 5.2 group 2). Same `alzheimers_disease`
test as Custom_AD_Dx_Guard, re-run after the wellness encounter has opened,
to catch an alzheimers.json diagnosis that landed during the wellness wait.
Everything that does the damage sits downstream of here -- Dementia_CarePlan,
FirstPrescription*, and (via ModerateDecline's PriorState branch) the whole
ModeratelySevere arm including EndFirstPrescription -- so a hit here closes
the chronic-ChEI strip and the duplicate care pathway completely, in both
orderings.
HONEST LIMIT, and the one thing this gate CANNOT undo: State.Encounter.process
calls diagnosePastConditions BEFORE handing control to this state, so a
patient who reaches here already had AlzheimersOnset diagnosed onto the
record. Because conditionStart is idempotent that adds no second row, but
State.ConditionOnset.diagnose does `entry.name = this.name` on the entry it
gets back, renaming alzheimers.json's shared 26929004 entry to
'AlzheimersOnset', and it sets `Type of Alzheimer's` to that entry.
The rename used to break alzheimers.json's Death_From_Alzheimers, which
resolved its cause of death by scanning for entry.name == 'MildDementia';
task 5.2 re-pointed that state at its `alzheimers_disease` attribute, which
holds the Entry object and survives the rename, so the residual is now
cosmetic. Exposure: only patients whose alzheimers.json diagnosis falls
inside the wellness-wait window (order 0.1% of the 65+ population).
Fixing it properly would mean making this module's diagnosis encounter
non-wellness, which changes ambulatory encounter volume -- out of scope
for a coordination task.
Releases the wellness encounter when Custom_AD_Dx_Recheck hands the patient
to alzheimers.json. Mirrors End_Diagnosis_Encounter but goes to Terminal
instead of ModerateDecline, so none of the downstream prescribing or
MedicationEnd states can be reached. Ending it is required rather than
optional: State.EncounterEnd clears this module's ACTIVE_WELLNESS_ENCOUNTER
key, and skipping it would leave the module holding a wellness check-in it
never releases.
The maximum MMSE score is 30 points. A score of 20 to 24 suggests mild dementia,
13 to 20 suggests moderate dementia, and less than 12 indicates severe dementia
http://www.alz.org/alzheimers_disease_steps_to_diagnosis.asp
also available is the Clinical Dementia Rating (CDR)
http://alzheimer.wustl.edu/cdr/cdr.htm

Task 2.11 (sweep): was condition_onset: "Pneumonia", at risk of the
renamed-entry null-cause bug -- 233604007 is also ConditionOnset'd
by cerebral_palsy.json, covid19/outcomes.json, pneumonia.json, and
primary_immunodeficiency.json, each under a different state name,
and HealthRecord.conditionStart is idempotent per code, so
whichever of those fires last on a comorbid patient renames the
shared present-map entry away from 'Pneumonia' and this state's
condition_onset scan silently records a null cause.
Sweep fix round 1 CORRECTION: the first pass converted this to
referenced_by_attribute: "hospice_reason", on the false claim that
hospice_reason was 'this module's existing assign_to_attribute ...
its only writer tree-wide'. It is not -- hospice_reason is the
tree's shared hospice-routing contract: alzheimers.json,
colorectal_cancer.json, home_hospice_snf.json (9 separate writers),
congestive_heart_failure.json, lung_cancer.json, breast_cancer.json,
and copd.json all SetAttribute it via value_attribute, by design,
so it can be legitimately reassigned to a different condition's
entry after Pneumonia sets it here. A comorbid patient whose other
disease module writes hospice_reason during the
PneumoniaEncounter->PneumoniaDeath window (4-14 days) would have
this Death misattributed to that other condition instead of
pneumonia -- the same silent-misattribution failure mode this
task exists to close, just via a shared attribute instead of a
renamed present-map entry. The Pneumonia ConditionOnset state
above already spends its one assign_to_attribute slot on
hospice_reason (for the hospice-routing contract, which is correct
and unrelated to this fix), so referenced_by_attribute isn't
available for cause-of-death use here. Uses the static codes form
instead: always populates reason, doesn't depend on any attribute
or present-map entry, immune to both failure classes. Loses no
patient-specific precision (233604007 is the only pneumonia code
this module ever onsets).
